context: Fix the comparison in the two query families -- build native date/datetime literals rather than strings -- then confirm at SF0.01 with polars-df. Check flightdata for the same pattern while there, since its gate is blocked on what sounds like the identical problem. Wiring a cross-surface gate for nyctaxi and tsbs_devops afterwards is the durable guard, and belongs to cross-surface-gate-rollout-followups rather than here.
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-24 on develop plus PR #1866. Once DataFrame query resolution reaches the registries these two families ship (previously it did not, so nothing executed and the defect was invisible):

  nyctaxi      3 of 75 pass, exit 1
  tsbs_devops  0 of 54 pass, exit 1

Every failure carries the same Polars error:
  cannot compare 'date/datetime/time' to a string value (create native python { 'date', 'datetime', 'time' } or compare to ...)

So the DataFrame implementations compare a temporal column against a string literal instead of a native date/datetime. One class of defect across both families, not many.

The other five previously-unreachable families are clean at the same scale: amplab 24/24, coffeeshop 33/33, h2odb 30/30, ssb 39/39, tpch_skew 66/66.

The correlation is informative. amplab, coffeeshop, h2odb and ssb are covered by ENFORCED cross-surface equivalence gates and all pass. nyctaxi, tsbs_devops and tpch_skew have no gate; two of those three are broken and the third is unverified. This is direct evidence for the breadth rollout tracked in cross-surface-gate-rollout-followups.

Note the same class is already recorded elsewhere: wire-the-flightdata-cross-surface-gate is blocked 'once its DataFrame date window is fixed'.

uv run -- benchbox run --platform polars-df --benchmark tsbs_devops --scale 0.01 --non-interactive
